findings.reason: a single-state field cannot represent that fixture, so the node must invent a second state axis or fail the gate the section set for itself.
findings.text: §4's mechanism gives each link "one state" from {in flight, ready-idle, gated, waiting}, but its done-when requires iter-switched-terminal-transients#s6 to read as gated on g-istt-6 and waiting on shared-coil-supply-model#s9 simultaneously

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §4's "reckon-a1" and §7's "the monitor plan" name no plan, section or commit that a later reader can open, though every href and file/section anchor cited resolves.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §2's headline done-when states a statement that is true by construction and names no fixture, so it cannot fail.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — no section places a gate log or evidence under a scratchpad or node-local temp path; §8 records into the plan's evidence by the repository convention.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the proposed surfaces ("board", ready-idle set, tiers) carry no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag, and §2 states its staleness window is a configuration value rather than a literal.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §4's mechanism gives each critical-path link one state, but its own done-when requires one link to read as two states at once.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each section names one deliverable (one read, one record, one measurement), and §7's two skill edits serve the one goal of pointing both skills at the bounded reads.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §5 and §6 both consume §3's ready-idle answer, but neither declares a depends-on edge to s3 in `plan-section-depends-on` (plan.html:23).
